title: The stricter border keeps fewer PTEN events (it was drawn around the controls)
plain: The 10% grace border keeps 89–94% of a control's Halo events but 70–90% of a PTEN mouse's.
how: Halo set = the loosest event border (4,824 events). 10% grace set = a border drawn around the control pool with 10% grace (4,201 events). Each Halo event is looked for in the 10% grace set by its time (within 5 ms). Per recording: the share kept.
ylabel:
Share of Halo events
the 10% grace border keeps
why: Every high-knockout mouse is below every control (P = 0.001); rho −0.75 with knockout; q (family) = 0.04, one of the few numbers that pass a correction within its family. It says PTEN dentate spikes more often fall outside the control-shaped cloud.
against: Largely by construction: the border was fitted to control events, so anything unlike controls is dropped. Tracks the year of recording (rho +0.64): the 2025 controls helped define the border. It shows PTEN events differ, not how.
test: Draw the border on half the controls and test the held-out controls against PTEN; or draw it on the pooled data blind to group.

title: The events the border drops are the lower-blade-heavy ones in IED+
plain: What the stricter border throws away in IED+ mice is mostly events whose lower blade's sink is much larger than the upper's.
how: Halo events outside the 10% grace border (matched by time). Per event: blade balance (upper − lower) / (upper + lower) of the sinks at the two blade sink rows, ±3 ms. Per recording: median over the dropped events.
ylabel:
Blade balance of the dropped events
(below 0 = lower blade's sink larger)
why: IED+ −0.68 to −0.12 against controls −0.14 to +0.13 (IED+ against control P = 0.010; trend P = 0.008). So the border partly removes exactly the events that carry leads 2 and 7: those leads are not made by the loose border, and a strict border weakens them.
against: A border drawn around control events will drop events unlike controls; this shows which ones. Tracks the year of recording (rho +0.48).
test: Run leads 2 and 7 on all detected events with no border.

title: The dropped events also carry the weaker source with knockout
plain: Among the events the stricter border drops, the net source between the blades falls with knockout, as it does over all events (lead 5).
how: Halo events outside the 10% grace border. Per event: mean CSD over the rows between the blade sink rows, ±3 ms, divided by the sink size. Per recording: median over the dropped events. Contrast: rank correlation with knockout within PTEN.
ylabel:
Net CSD between the blades / sink size
(dropped events, median)
why: Within PTEN rho = −0.80 (P = 0.014), the same as over kept events (rho −0.77): lead 5 does not depend on which border is used.
against: Dropped events are few in some mice (6–30% of a recording). Nine PTEN mice in two knockout clusters.

title: The P-spike filter removes events almost only in IED+ mice
plain: The few events that also sit inside the P-spike border (24 in all) come mostly from IED+ mice.
how: 10% grace set against No P-spikes set: an event is removed when it also lies inside the P-spike (IED) border. Per recording: the share of the 10% grace events removed.
ylabel: Share of events removed as P-spikes
why: 4 of 5 IED+ mice lose events (0.8–3.4%), against 1 of 7 controls and 1 of 4 IED− mice; IED+ against control P = 0.030. A sanity check that the lab's IED label and the P-spike border agree, and a hint that in IED+ mice some dentate spikes grade into P-spikes.
against: 24 events in total; most mice lose none, so ranks are full of ties.
test: Count P-spike-like dentate spikes on all detected events with one fixed P-spike rule.

title: With no minimum type size, DS2's source is briefer with knockout (DS3 removed)
plain: Dropping the 5% minimum type size makes lead 8 stronger: the source of DS2 events is briefer the higher the knockout.
how: No-cutoff filter: the optimized-curve classifier is used however small its smaller type is, and a type counts with any number of events. DS2 events, DS3 taken out. Per event: the source trace (CSD at the source rows) and its width at half height (ms). Per recording: median. Contrast: rank correlation with knockout within PTEN.
ylabel:
Source duration, DS2 without DS3
(no minimum type size; median, ms)
why: Within PTEN rho = −0.99 (P = 0.000004; other event set P = 0.00007); under P 0.05 with 15 of 20 classifiers; q (family) = 0.06. The strongest dose relation in the battery.
against: Over all events the relation is not there (P = 0.84). Whole-millisecond durations, so ties decide ranks. Tracks the year of recording (rho +0.49). Eight PTEN mice have a value.
test: Duration on the mean DS2 per mouse at 30 kHz; one planned Spearman test within PTEN in new mice.
